CAVEATThe perfect-arbitrage / continuous-time assumption underlying Merton's models holds only in calm markets; it stops holding once markets become discontinuous, so any strategy that relies on continuous rebalancing is only valid in quiet conditions.69
CAVEATThe Black-Scholes framework assumes volatility is a constant, inherent trait of a security; when volatility itself is unstable, option pricing and any volatility-linked trading logic built on it loses its foundation.68
CAVEATEven a supposedly low-risk spread/arbitrage bet is not risk-free, and leverage multiplies the penalty for being wrong, so any leveraged low-margin strategy has a hard tail-risk constraint.52
CAVEATIlliquidity is only a problem when you may be forced to sell quickly; a leveraged book is exactly the situation where illiquid positions become dangerous because losses accumulate fast.100
CAVEATFinancial markets involve both quantifiable risk and non-quantifiable uncertainty, unlike dice; the uncertainty component cannot be modeled with precise odds, so any method that assigns exact probabilities to market outcomes overstates its precision.63
CAVEATMathematical modeling attaches false certainty to events that are inherently uncertain, so quantified strategies should not be trusted at their face-value confidence levels.75
CAVEATMeasuring risk is not the same as eliminating it; risk quantification gives no protection against the risk materializing, so measurable-risk methods do not remove downside.116
CAVEATEven a firm that pioneered risk-modeling admits the models may give a greater sense of security than warranted and says reliance on them should be limited.234
CAVEATCombining high leverage with illiquidity forces a strategy to be right every single day, not just on the final horizon; one wrong day ends the position, so such a structure is only viable if the edge wins daily.233
SCOPE_LIMITUnlike actuarial data, market samples are never known to be complete and the underlying distribution changes across regimes, so historical-sample statistics on markets are not dependable for forecasting.71
SCOPE_LIMITIn paired-share / relative-value trades there is no known 'correct' premium, and the spread can persist or widen against the model for as long as it likes, so convergence timing is not bounded.99
SCOPE_LIMITCorrelation assumptions break down in stress: during crises, unrelated assets become more tightly linked and move together, undermining any diversification or correlation-based hedging built on calm-period data.122
SCOPE_LIMITShort-volatility trading relies on the assumption that volatility is consistent over time and reverts to a normal range; that assumption is exactly what broke the fund, so volatility-reversion strategies are bounded by regime behavior.123
SCOPE_LIMITA method only applies where the trader has an informational or structural advantage; directional trades outside the model's expertise area (here: a small currency) are outside the strategy's scope.128
SCOPE_LIMITA strategy that succeeded in one market does not transfer to another where the firm lacks expertise; entering an unfamiliar arena at scale adds unmodeled risk.101
SCOPE_LIMITMarkets are not independent random draws like coin flips: they have memory and can trend because traders expect them to, so independence-based statistics (random-walk assumptions) do not apply.73
SCOPE_LIMITThe over-the-counter volatility market is structurally imbalanced (many buyers, few sellers), so a short-vol position can face a one-sided market where the price can move arbitrarily against it; exit and mark-to-market are at the counterparties' discretion.125
FAILURE_EXAMPLEPortfolio insurance, a continuous-time hedging strategy marketed as a loss limiter, failed exactly on Black Monday when the market gapped: the hedging rule forced continuous selling that worsened the crash and its users lost their shirts.69
FAILURE_EXAMPLEValue-at-Risk-type risk programs performed in normal times but failed in Mexico in 1995, precisely at the moments of unexpected turbulence when protection was needed most.76
FAILURE_EXAMPLEIn August-September 1998 every one of the fund's trades lost simultaneously because correlations went to one; the modelers had assumed normal distributions would produce offsetting outcomes, and they were wrong.175
FAILURE_EXAMPLEThe fund lost 44% of its value in August 1998 alone (52% year-to-date), a magnitude the partners themselves called a shock given the historical volatility of the fund; the model's loss distribution was breached massively.161
FAILURE_EXAMPLERussia's 1998 default was an event the market treated as impossible (a nuclear power would not default); when it happened, markets seized up, and the whole set of assumptions built on the implicit safety net collapsed.146
FAILURE_EXAMPLEWhile the fund claimed it was reducing risk, its leverage had actually risen to 55-to-1 (a fact withheld from investors), showing that declared risk-reduction measures were not being executed.162
FAILURE_EXAMPLEThe fund's risk-aggregator exposure numbers rested on assuming swap-spread volatility of only 8 points a year, an assumption that was already false in 1998 when spreads had moved 40 points, so the headline risk numbers were meaningless.188
FAILURE_EXAMPLECollateral posted against derivative positions only protects if one party sells alone; if all counterparties try to exit simultaneously in a failure, the collateral itself plummets in value, so collateral-based protection fails in a systemic exit.188
FAILURE_EXAMPLEFinancing without haircuts let a leveraged fund operate right at the edge of solvency, so a default could wipe it out entirely; the absence of margin cushions made the collapse total.179
FAILURE_EXAMPLEThe fund's model expected August losses to be recovered via diversification; diversification failed and the losses continued, so portfolio diversification across correlated trades provided no protection.181
FAILURE_EXAMPLEDynamic hedging, the strategy Merton's model prescribed, amplified the 1997 crash: systematic selling as markets fell made a bad day worse, showing hedging rules that sell into declines are destabilizing.117
FAILURE_EXAMPLEA short on a company whose components cannot be bought (because assets are private) is a one-sided, poorly conceived arbitrage: the convergence leg does not exist, so the trade is unhedgeable.129
FAILURE_EXAMPLEA large short position in a thin OTC market with only a few dealers can be cornered: dealers refused to sell, trapping the short and driving the price up, so exit became impossible.176
REFUTATIONFama's empirical finding directly refutes the normal distribution: price moves beyond five standard deviations occur about once every three to four years rather than once every 7,000 years, so fat tails are routine in markets.72
REFUTATIONThe book's core refutation of the fund's method: the professors knew but ignored that market return tails are always fat, i.e., extreme events are far more frequent than the models allowed for.175
REFUTATIONValue-at-Risk is dismissed as a false beacon: it gives a sense of security to those about to be destroyed, i.e., it does not actually protect against the disasters it claims to measure.76
REFUTATIONThe efficient market hypothesis, the intellectual foundation for the fund's models, is dismissed by a senior economist as the most remarkable error in the history of economic theory.74
REFUTATIONThe author refutes the entire paradigm of inferring tomorrow's risk from yesterday's prices and volatilities, calling it Long-Term's basic mistake and a flaw at the heart of modern finance.234
REFUTATIONModels cannot forecast the limits of market behavior because they assume reasonable participants; traders are not always reasonable, so model-based boundaries on how far prices can go are invalid.234
REFUTATIONThe Keynes epigraph refutes mean-reversion timing: prices can stay irrational longer than a leveraged trader can stay solvent, so betting on reversion without the capital to outlast the mispricing fails.123
REFUTATIONAcademic research (Shleifer-Vishny) refutes the assumption that arbitrage reliably corrects mispricing: noise traders can push prices further away, and an arbitrageur can be forced to liquidate at market lows precisely when the mispricing is largest.111
REFUTATIONThe fund's models implied losing all capital required a ten-sigma event (probability ~10^-24); this confidence was refuted when the fund lost nearly all its capital within months, showing sigma-based impossibility claims are meaningless.128
CONTRADICTIONThe fund's own investor letter claimed losses over 20% should happen at most one year in fifty and did not entertain larger losses, yet the fund lost 44% in a single month.63
CONTRADICTIONThe fund's diversification claim (global spread of eggs means no single market can hurt it) contradicts the book's conclusion that all baskets broke simultaneously.36
REFUTATIONDiversification in form without diversification in substance fails: the fund had effectively made the same bet (on lower-rated bonds) everywhere, so all positions fell in lockstep when the credit cycle turned.233

  • G/F/X track'leri işlenmedi. 2432 claim (risk geometrisi, metodoloji, execution) hiçbir işleme aşamasına girmemiştir. Sistem kurulumunu besleyen asıl malzeme burada ve eksik (P5_GXF_TASK.md).

Bu belgedeki eşleşme yapısal bir harita — "bu alan gelecekte bu veriyle beslenecek" demektir, "zaten besleniyor" değil.
